review.reason:
Candidate 35 passes selection on its current numbered geometry.

Hole 1: The 481-yard par 5 combines a substantial left-side lake with a pronounced right turn and collision trees inside the corner. Following the fairway provides a credible staged route; attempting to shorten the hole brings the wooded corner and approach bunker into play. Greenside sand sits right and back-left, leaving the front accessible. The corridor is demanding without looking unreasonably squeezed.

Hole 2: The dry 413-yard par 4 has genuinely separate routes around a central tree strip, with a bunker near its lower end. The broader right branch offers forgiveness, while the left branch provides a different approach alignment. Both reconnect before the green, whose back-left bunkers leave an open front. The generous fairway makes this the round's recovery opportunity, but the collision-tree divider prevents it from being merely an undifferentiated wide hole.

Hole 3: The 174-yard par 3 has one substantial lake surrounding an elongated island green, plus a separate foreground landing area and left-side bunker. Center-green play offers a sensible alternative to attacking the left-positioned pin; the shorter length makes the forced carry reasonable.

The par-5/4/3 progression, wooded dogleg, dry split route and island target provide excellent within-round contrast. The island repeats course 93, but at a shorter distance; the dogleg-right and split-fairway holes introduce types absent from all three recent rounds. Simulated 2/2/1 shots to green and 55/148/26 safe tee options support, rather than prove, the visible playability. No geometry edits are needed at selection; artwork correspondence remains to be reviewed after generation.
